body: Shouldn't you have the instance data creation inside the while loop?

At the end of the loop, `_add_to_batch` actually copies the bytes out of the 'new instance data' and into the stored buffer. 

``` c++
memcpy(&state.instance_data[state.instance_data_index], &state.intermediary_instance_data, sizeof(InstanceData));
```

So it saves us a little bit of time to just setup the buffer outside of the loop, and overwrite it + copy out each step, rather than set up a new buffer each step.

`MultiRect` was intended to be a fixed size type so it can be stored on the stack. There is a final allocation (even in 3.x) for copying to the command, but `Vector` is super heavyweight for bottleneck operations like appending etc.

`FixedVector` is the 4.x version that @Ivorforce made which is basically like `FixedArray` in 3.x (if I remember right).
`FixedVector` is fixed capacity and variable size. We could also merge `FixedArray` for fixed capacity and fixed size if desirable.

Yeah I could have equally called `FixedArray` `FixedVector` as it does the same job.

The distinction was from a `DynamicArray`. When I see `Vector` it makes me think of dynamic allocations, which is probably why I avoided it at the time, but it's just as good or better a name.

`FixedVector` would work perfectly here as a slot in replacement I think.

BTW @ColinSORourke be sure to profile this stuff, as it is bottleneck code and it will pretty soon show when there are performance issues introduced.

Another thing that occurred to me .. it's possible some care may be needed in 4.x as it is rather more multithreaded than 4.x, just in case of multiple threads trying to fill the same `MultiRect` from the client code, so that's worth double checking there aren't any differences needed compared to how it's done in 3.x, maybe by running it in asan while hammering it in multithread mode.

I can't remember if there was similar in 3.x, but calculating this bounding rect can be done as a one-off on creating the `MultiRect` I suspect, rather than calculating here (*if* it is done every frame).

Maybe it isn't done every frame though, worth checking, as it seems unlikely I would have missed this making the 3.x PR. :thinking: 

(A lot of the benefit of `MultiRect` is moving the processing to a one-off on creation, rather than doing it in batching every frame.)

Ah, by `FixedArray` I meant my [open PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106928) for it, not the 3.x `FixedArray`. It's a separate implemention, which (like mentioned) has both a fixed capacity and a fixed size.

I am mainly bringing this up because it doesn't match the other usages of `new_instance_data` function. The amount of `new_instance_data` and `_add_to_batch` calls always match up.

Also, the line you mentioned was added in #115757, so before that PR, this approach would not actually work.

If you want to keep this, I'd recommend adding a comment explaining why you are reusing the instance data for multiple `_add_to_batch` calls.

Is there a workaround for declaring a `FixedVector` in a C++ Header? Rects & Sources have to be Private Variables of the `MultiRect` struct, and when I try and make them `FixedVector<Rect2, 2048>`, the engine will not compile because the `FixedVector` definition includes a Constant Expression and "Statement expression not allowed at file scope"

If I understand correctly, having a Fixed Variable of a struct requires `FixedArray` rather than `FixedVector` because this has to do with the Variable Size of a `FixedVector` is incompatible with being in a header
@Ivorforce pinging for above, I'm not sure what is going on there with `FixedVector`.

Yup, or you can calculate the bound during adding each rect on the client side.

It might depend which thread is more bottlenecked (main thread versus render thread, if this is multithreaded?). Might be worth some experimentation, but I doubt it matters much either way as expanding a bound is pretty cheap.

I'll actually look at doing this in 3.x, must have missed it for some reason (maybe it doesn't appear that high in profiles).

I've done a draft to add it in 3.x: #117007 , although interestingly `get_rect()` with `MultiRect` is not being called in the benchmark code with a label I used to develop the system.

I need to evaluate whether this path is actually being used in the wild (in 3.x) before making this change, as it will be deleterious if not. Same is true in 4.x (your tests seem to indicate it is used in 4.x, the culling is more primitive there).

UPDATE:
My tests so far have indicated it is not required in 3.x, due to the use of either custom bounds, or hierarchical culling (which caches bounds automatically). It may still be beneficial in 4.x, so will leave it to you to test this.
failing since it is a span here but a Vector in the header
i think the tilemap specific functionality should live with the tilemap node instead of in this general purpose helper

Flipside, there's a load of `MultiRect` specific stuff in there which would make the tilemap code much more difficult to read / maintain.

We don't want to end up in a situation where everyone touching the tilemap code has to cognitively process the multirect code.

For separation of concerns, I do suspect keeping it in the helper may be the lesser of two evils.
You should be able to use the `Span` constructor from `Vector` now without this definition.
